newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Catholic monastery comes under fire in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Catholic monastery comes under fire in Bosnia.

text.p: Three rifle grenades were fired at a Roman Catholic monastery in central Bosnia a week before a scheduled visit of Pope John Paul II to the capital Sarajevo, a U.N. spokesman said on Sunday.
One of the three grenades hit the monastery and two fell in a garden 25 metres (yards) away, said Andrea Angelli, a spokesman for U.N. police monitors.
The attack occurred at about 11:25 p.m. (2125 GMT) on Saturday night at a Franciscan monastery in Kraljeva Sutjeska, about 60 km (40 miles) north of Sarajevo, he said.
U.N. police monitors believed the grenades were fired from a hill about one kilomtere (mile) away from the monastery.
The blast shattered all 40 windows in the mediaeval monastery -- one of the oldest in Bosnia -- but no injuries were reported, a guardian at the monastery said.
The incident was the latest in a series of bomb attacks against churches and monasteries in recent months. Two mosques were also targetted.
None of the attacks has caused injuries and no one has claimed responsibility for the bombings, which have coincided with political tensions in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation.
The violence has raised concerns about security surrounding the Pope's historic visit to Sarajevo next Saturday and Sunday.
Bosnian Moslem authorities in the capital say they will deploy thousands of police and place severe restrictions on traffic during the 25-hour visit.
The 31,000-strong NATO-led peace force says local authorities are primarily responsible for security during the Papal visit.
Pope John Paul II planned to visit Sarajevo during the 1992-95 war but had to cancel his trip because of concern for his security.
